why: A type is read as it is whatever its depth, and a type that recurs on its own descent is read by the datatype name a record reserved, else opaque (design/types-depth.md). deepLeaf: the parameter is ten records deep (L0 to L8, then Line, then string | null); the candidate reads the same leaf through a local naming the fifth level: proved (at the base the depth bound refuses the type: no lemma). deepChanged: the candidate reads the leaf's sibling `other`: not proved; lane B witnesses a value whose two leaves differ. shapeOf: n8n's JsonValue, a union of primitives, a dictionary and an array of itself, is opaque before any descent (the base reads it so too); the candidate inverts the array test: proved. shapeChanged: the candidate calls an element nested when it is any object, an array of a JSON object among them: not proved; lane B witnesses [{}]. hasChild: Tree is a dictionary of itself, whose descent meets itself with no record between: opaque (at the base the depth bound refuses it); the candidate names the test first: proved. hasGrandchild: the candidate drops the test of a child's own keys: not proved; lane B witnesses a Tree with one empty child. second: Stream<string> is a callable returning a tuple holding itself: opaque, and a call of it is a call of an opaque value (at the base refused); the parent names the first step, the candidate reads the rest from the call (every call is through a name: a computed callee is another rule): proved. secondChanged: the candidate reads the third head: not proved; lane B witnesses a stream whose heads differ.
